lesson.guided_practice:
PRACTISE BEFORE READING THE FEEDBACK
Order lightest to heaviest: 1.2 kg, 900 g, 0.95 kg.

FEEDBACK
900 g, 0.95 kg (950 g), 1.2 kg.

WATCH FOR
Comparing 900 and 1.2 without converting units can reverse the order.
lesson.independent_task:
INDEPENDENT EVIDENCE
Compare fourteen mass pairs (convert first) and order six sets of three. Record units every time.

Write a short reflection naming one step you corrected and why.

lesson.parent_notes:
Parent: Marking guidance for the independent task: Compare fourteen mass pairs (convert first) and order six sets of three. Record units every time. Accept equivalent original responses that show the same skill.

Parent: Written model 1: Sample: new numbers solved with visible working for measure; key places/values named. Do not award marks for retyping the model.

Parent: Written model 2: Sample misconception: Comparing 900 and 1.2 without converting units can reverse the order.. Correction uses 900 g, 0.95 kg (950 g), 1.2 kg.. Why: restores accurate measure.

Parent: Likely misconception: Comparing 900 and 1.2 without converting units can reverse the order. Keep sample answers out of the child role.

Parent: Short-answer focus 1: Solve one fresh problem that uses measure with different numbers from the worked model. Show working and name the places or values that matter.

Parent: Short-answer focus 2: Describe one likely mistake with measure, show corrected working, and say why the correction works.

Parent: Marking notes: Accept any mathematically valid solution that uses new numbers, shows working for measure, and names places/values. Reject copied model numbers. / Accept a named misconception about measure, corrected working, and a method reason. Reject vague “I was wrong” with no repair..

teach_steps.example:
WORKED MODEL

teach_steps.explain:
Measuring and comparing mass uses scales or balance ideas; order objects and record with units.

WHY IT MATTERS
This helps the learner choose methods based on place value, quantity and accurate working, rather than guessing digits by shape alone. Keep every step justified.

HOW TO WORK
Read the worked example and name the places, values or distances that carry the method. Before looking at the correction, make your own attempt using the exact question provided. Compare your working with the feedback: did you use the same skill and show your reasoning? If a digit or place is uncertain, identify what would have to be regrouped or counted again. One deliberate, justified revision is more useful than writing a longer answer.
